---
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
(\cite{A:POG})
Let ${\pazocal{A}}$ be a free projective line arrangement. Then by adding or deleting a line one obtains either a free or a POG arrangement.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
(\cite{M})
 Given a free curve, by the addition or deletion of a smooth conic, as an irreducible component, one necessarily obtains a curve of type at most $2$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm: gen_exp}
\begin{enumerate}
\item ${\mathcal{C}}$ is free if and only if  $t({\mathcal{C}}) =0$.                    
\item ${\mathcal{C}}$ is plus-one generated if and only if $t({\mathcal{C}})=1$.                  
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
(\cite[Lemma 3.1]{dPW})
\label{lem:3.1}
Let $\{ \theta^0_1, \theta^0_2\}  \subset D_0({\mathcal{C}})$ homogeneous derivations, $$\theta^0_1 = a_1 \partial x + b_1 \partial y +c_1 \partial z, \; \theta^0_2 = a_2 \partial x + b_2 \partial y +c_2 \partial z.$$ Then there exists $h \in S$ such that  $$(b_1 c_2 - b_2 c_1, c_1 a_2 - c_2 a_1,  a_1 b_2 -a_2 b_1) = h(\frac{\partial f_{{\mathcal{C}}}}{\partial x}, \frac{\partial f_{{\mathcal{C}}}}{\partial y}, \frac{\partial f_{{\mathcal{C}}}}{\partial z}).$$
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:det}
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $\{\theta^0_1, \theta^0_2, \theta^0_3 \} \subset D_0({\mathcal{C}})$ homogeneous derivations,  $$\det M(\theta^0_1, \theta^0_2, \theta^0_3)=0.$$
\item For $\{ \theta^0_1, \theta^0_2\}  \subset D_0({\mathcal{C}})$ homogeneous derivations, there exists $g \in S$ such that 
$$\det M(\theta_E, \theta^0_1, \theta^0_2) = g f_{{\mathcal{C}}}.$$
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Immediate from Lemma \ref{lem:3.1}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:Delta|f}
For any  set of homogeneous derivations $\{ \theta_1, \theta_2, \theta_3\} \subset D({\mathcal{C}})$, there exists $g \in S$ such that  
$$
\det M(\theta_1, \theta_2, \theta_3) = gf_{{\mathcal{C}}}.
$$
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Since $\theta_i \in D({\mathcal{C}})$, there exists $g_i \in S$ such that $\theta_i(f_{{\mathcal{C}}}) = g_i f_{{\mathcal{C}}}, \; i=\overline{1,3}$.
Write, as in \eqref{eq:theta_0}, $\theta_i = \theta^0_i +d^{-1} g_i \theta_E$. Then $M(\theta_1, \theta_2, \theta_3)  = M(\theta^0_1 + d^{-1} g _1 \theta_E, \theta^0_2 + d^{-1} g _2 \theta_E, \theta^0_3 + d^{-1} g _3 \theta_E),$ so, by basic properties of determinants,
$$\det M(\theta_1, \theta_2, \theta_3) = \det M(\theta^0_1, \theta^0_2, \theta^0_3) + \sum_{i<j} \pm  d^{-2}g_ig_j\det M(\theta_E, \theta^0_i, \theta^0_j)$$ 
 The claim now follows from Corollary \ref{cor:det}.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:lemmas_extended_to_curves}
 Let  $\{\theta_1, \cdots ,\theta_4 \} \subset D({\mathcal{C}})$ be homogeneous derivations and denote $g_i:=(-1)^ig_{1 \cdots \hat{i} \cdots 4}.$
 Then 
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item $\sum_{i=1}^4 g_i \theta_i =0$.
 \item If $g_i \neq 0$, then, for any $\theta \in D({\mathcal{C}})$, $g_i \theta \in \langle \theta_1, \dots \hat{\theta_i}, \cdots , \theta_4 \rangle$.
 \item If there is a relation of type $\sum_{j \neq i} f_j \theta_j + g_i \theta =0$, then the coefficients $f_j \in S$ are uniquely determined by the identity                           
 $(-1)^j \det M( \theta_1, \cdots \hat{\theta_j}, \cdots,  \theta_4, \theta)=f_j f_{{\mathcal{C}}}.$
 \end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
(\cite{Chu})
\label{thm:Chu-thm_1.4}
Let ${\pazocal{A}}$ be an arrangement of projective lines. Then ${\pazocal{A}}$ is SPOG  and the set $\{\theta_1, \cdots, \theta_4\}$ is a minimal generating system for $D({\pazocal{A}})$ that satisfies the minimal degree relation $\sum_{i=1}^4  g_i \theta_i =0$ if and only if $0 \neq g_4 \in S_1$ and $g_1, g_2, g_3 \in S_{>0}$ have no non-trivial divisor modulo $g_4$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:Chu_thm_consequence}
Let ${\mathcal{C}}$ be a non-free curve.  Then ${\mathcal{C}}$ is POG if and only if there exists a set of homogeneous derivations $\{\theta_1, \theta_2, \theta_3 \} \subset D({\mathcal{C}})$  such that $0 \neq g_{123} \in S_1$.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Let us prove first the direct implication. If ${\mathcal{C}}$ is POG with generalized  exponents $(1,d_2,d_3, d_4)$ then choose from a minimal system of generators for $D({\mathcal{C}})$ three homogeneous derivations $\theta_1, \theta_2, \theta_3$, such that $\deg(\theta_1) =1$, $\deg(\theta_2) =d_2$ and $\deg(\theta_3) =d_3$. 
 Recall that, since ${\mathcal{C}}$ is POG, we have the identity $d_2+d_3 = \deg({\mathcal{C}})$. Then $\deg(g_{123}) = 1+d_2+d_3 - \deg({\mathcal{C}}) = 1$. Moreover, since $\theta_1, \theta_2, \theta_3$ are S-independent, $g_{123} \neq 0$.
 \smallskip
 
 Conversely, assume that ${\mathcal{C}}$ is non-free and such that there exists a set of homogeneous derivations $\{\theta_1, \theta_2, \theta_3\} \subset D({\mathcal{C}})$ with $0 \neq g_{123} \in S_1$.  The condition $0 \neq g_{123}$ implies that the derivations $\theta_1, \theta_2, \theta_3$ are $S$-independent and the condition $g_{123} \in S_1$ implies that $\deg(\theta_1) + \deg(\theta_2) + \deg(\theta_3) = d+1$.  Keeping in mind that $\theta_1, \theta_2, \theta_3$ are $S$-independent, if $1 \leq d_2 \leq \cdots \leq d_r$ denote the generalized exponents of ${\mathcal{C}}$, then the following inequality holds  
 $$\deg(\theta_1) + \deg(\theta_2) + \deg(\theta_3) \geq 1+d_2+d_3,$$
  hence $d+1 \geq 1+d_2+d_3$. Since ${\mathcal{C}}$ is not free, this implies, by Theorem \ref{thm: gen_exp}, that ${\mathcal{C}}$ must necessarily be POG.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:counter}
 \cite[Conjecture 4.2]{Chu}, which states  that, for a projective line arrangement ${\pazocal{A}}$, a resolution of $D({\pazocal{A}})$ is necessarily of the following type
$$0 \rightarrow  \bigoplus_{i=2}^{r-2} S[-d_{i+2}-1] \rightarrow  \bigoplus_{i=1}^{r} S[-d_i] \rightarrow D({\mathcal{C}}) \rightarrow 0 $$ 
does not hold for curves.  It also does not hold for arrangements of projective lines (equivalently, central arrangements of planes in $\mathbb{C}^3$). Any type $2A$ curve or projective line arrangement is a counterexample.  See for instance \cite[Theorems 3.1, 3.3 and Remarks 3.3, 3.7]{M} for a recipe to construct such counterexamples, by addition-deletion of a smooth conic to a free curve.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
${\mathcal{C}}:  (x^2 + 2xy + y^2 + xz)(x^2 + xz + yz)(x^2 + xy + z^2)(x+y-z)y(x+z)(2x+y)(x^2 + 2xy - xz + yz)=0$ is a type $2A$ curve with generalized exponents $(1,6,7,7)$, which can be obtained by deletion of a smooth conic from a free curve, see  \cite[Example 4.4]{M}.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:indeg}
\begin{enumerate}
\item  $Indeg J(G)  = t({\mathcal{C}})$
\item  $J(G) = J(G^0)$
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
(1) This is obvious, since $t({\mathcal{C}}) = Indeg B({\mathcal{C}}, \theta^0_2) = 1+d_2+d_3-d$ and $G$ is a minimal generating set for $D({\mathcal{C}})$, where the degree $d$ curve ${\mathcal{C}}$ has generalized exponents  $1 \leq d_2 \leq \cdots \leq d_r$.

(2) It is enough to notice that $\det M(\theta_1, \theta_j, \theta_k) = \det M(\theta_1, \theta^0_j, \theta^0_k)$ and $g_{ijk} \in \langle g_{ij}, g_{jk}, g_{ik} \rangle$, for any $i,j,k \geq 2$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
In general, if $G$ is a system of generators for $D({\mathcal{C}})$,  $B({\mathcal{C}}, \theta^0_2) \subsetneq J(G)$.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- prop-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:type_leq2_char}
 ${\mathcal{C}}$ is of type at most $k$ if and only if there exists $H \subset D({\mathcal{C}})$ such that $Indeg(J(H))=k$.
<!-- end prop-3 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
Let $H \subset D({\mathcal{C}})$ be such that $Indeg(J(H))=2$. If ${\mathcal{C}}$ is free or POG, then $H$ cannot be a system of generators for $D({\mathcal{C}})$.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:non_rel_thetaE23}
If $\{\theta_E, \theta_2, \theta_3 , \cdots, \theta_r\}$ is a minimal generating system of $ D({\mathcal{C}})$ such that $1 \leq \deg(\theta_2) \leq \deg(\theta_3) \leq \cdots \leq \deg(\theta_r)$, then there is no non-trivial relation that involves only $\{\theta_E, \theta_2, \theta_3\}$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Assume to the contrary that there is a relation $\alpha_E \theta_E + \alpha_2 \theta_2 + \alpha_3 \theta_3 =0$, $\alpha_E, \alpha_2, \alpha_3 \in S$. Since $D({\mathcal{C}}) = D_0({\mathcal{C}}) \oplus S \theta_E$ , the relation implies that $\alpha_2 \theta^0_2 + \alpha_3 \theta^0_3 =0$, where $\theta_i := \theta^0_i + \deg( f_{{\mathcal{C}}})^{-1} g  \theta_E, \; i=2,3$, see \eqref{eq:theta_0}. Let $\alpha = \gcd(\alpha_2,  \alpha_3)$. Then there exist $\alpha'_2,  \alpha'_3 \in S, \; \gcd(\alpha'_2,  \alpha'_3) = 1$ and $\alpha_2 = \alpha \alpha'_2, \alpha_3 = \alpha \alpha'_3$. Hence $\alpha'_3$ divides $\theta^0_2 $, i.e. there exists $\theta^{01}_2 \in D_0({\mathcal{C}})$ such that  $\theta^0_2 = \alpha'_3 \theta^{01}_2$. If $\deg(\alpha'_3) > 0$ that would contradict the minimality of the degree of $\theta^0_2$, which is supposed to be $mdr(f_{{\mathcal{C}}})$. So necessarily $\alpha'_3 \in \mathbb{C}^*$. But then $ \theta^0_2, \theta^0_3$ are S-dependent, which contradicts the minimality of the generating system. In conclusion a relation of type $\alpha_E \theta_E + \alpha_2 \theta_2 + \alpha_3 \theta_3 =0$ must have zero coefficients.\\
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
\label{rem:rel_2B}
If  ${\mathcal{C}}$ is a type $2B$ curve, say, with minimal generating system for  $D({\mathcal{C}})$ consisting of the degree ordered derivations $\{\theta_E, \theta_2, \theta_3, \theta_4, \theta_5\}$ then, by Lemma \ref{lem:non_rel_thetaE23}, the two generating syzygies of degrees $e_2,e_3$ (see \eqref{eq:res_arb_curve}) necessarily involve terms with non-trivial coefficients for either  $\theta_4$ or  $\theta_5$.  
Consider the  \ref{prop:lemmas_extended_to_curves}(1) type relations for $\{\theta_E, \theta_2, \theta_3, \theta_4\}$, respectively $\{\theta_E, \theta_2, \theta_3, \theta_5\}$.  The (degree $2$) coefficients of $\theta_4, \theta_5$ in these relations are equal, up to $\mathbb{C}^*$, to $g_{123}$.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- question-1: body_md -->
It would be interesting to have a characterization of type $2$ curves along the lines of Theorem \ref{thm:Chu_thm_consequence}. The above computations from \ref{lem:non_rel_thetaE23} and \ref{rem:rel_2B} might be of relevance for this endeavour.
<!-- end question-1 -->
